To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

head-scatter factors increase with field size less quickly when build-up caps and miniphantoms of high atomic number are used, that ion chambers and diodes yield identical head-scatter factors when the same type build-up caps are employed, and that the use of column miniphantoms is a simple way to avoid contamination electrons in the measurement of head-scatter factor.

the scatter factors Sh, also referred as output factors, for dosimetry of photon beams in water are measured using a cylindrical build-up cap and a columnar miniphantom constructed from material with a density and an atomic number close that of water.
head-scatter factors measured with cylindrical build-up cups constructed of high atomic number materials are lower than those measured with build-up caps constructed of low atomic number materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of build-up caps and miniphantoms for the measurement of head-scatter and backscattering factors.
the determination of the head-scatter factors, which are measured in-air using cylindrical build-up caps or columnar miniphantom.
the development of a new technique for the measurement of head-scatter factor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the head-scatter factors, measured with a cylindrical build-up cap, are not suitable for the calculation of dose in water.

the head-scatter factor, Sh, should be measured with a cylindrical build-up cap of high-Z material, or a columnar miniphantom of high-Z material with a wall thickness in the transverse direction that is sufficient to prevent contamination electrons from entering the detector.
for accurate dosimetry, the use of a cylindrical build-up cap and columnar miniphaantom with the atomic number of the phantom material is recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sh increases with field sizes less rapidly with high-Z build-up caps and miniphantoms because of a net scatter effect of contamination electrons and a net scatter effect due to photon energy changes.
the choice of build-up cap and columnar phantom material should be based on the atomic number of the phantom material.
the head-scatter factors are independent of the detector and the build-up caps or columnar miniphantom used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sh values for a given field size are not unique and depend on the type of build-up cap used.
the Sh values measured in air with ion chambers or semiconductor diodes are different from those obtained in water.
the choice of the materials used to construct the build-up caps and miniphantoms has an important impact on the measured Sh.
